text: Not long after, frost creeps across the rooftop room from the bed, where Jaeha sits rigid, eyes glowing cyan, blood running from his nose.
Seoa shakes him. He's freezing! Nib holds her back. Don't pull him back. He's still on the Far Side.
Frost forms on his lashes.
In front of him, a small window. The call: twenty-two seconds left. Answers: zero.
Ten minutes earlier, the room is warm and ordinary, and Jaeha is writing fast.
A job advert. Wanted: one strong fighter. Pay: thirty percent of every core. Free ramen.
Seoa reads it, deadpan. He wrote a job advert. It worked on every guild that ever hired him.
Nib doesn't unfold his arms. They won't come for money. Nobody on the Far Side has anything left to buy.
Then he yanks the curtain shut on Gomi's face, pressed against the window.
Everyone wants something, Jaeha says. He just has to guess what.
So he asks: why did Nib answer him, that night? Because Jaeha was standing in front of someone.
And if something huge answers? This room is nine square metres. Then they'll need a bigger room.
Seoa holds up her stopwatch. He has to promise to come back. It isn't a gate, Jaeha says. It's a phone call.
He presses Call.
And he's standing on endless black water under a starless sky, ringed by tall glowing rifts, each a doorway somewhere else. One minute.
He turns slowly, taking them in.
A burning fortress under a great bell. A mossy field where a long hill seems to breathe. A river, a white ward, a frozen forest.
Through one, a tall archer stands on a riverbank, a long beaded braid over her shoulder.
Through another, a broad figure in surgeon's plate bends over a bed.
A window: speak your offer. Jaeha clears his throat.
And reads his advert aloud. Kang Jaeha, looking for one strong fighter. Thirty percent of every core, and the ramen is free.
The archer turns away, and voices drift over the water: another master who wants a weapon. He talks like a merchant.
Then the burning fortress flares. Beside a swinging bronze bell, a broad figure in bell-shaped armour turns toward him. Fifty-two seconds.
It hears him, it says. He is young, and he speaks like a merchant.
Jaeha steps forward eagerly. Then come through. He can negotiate.
The figure strikes its bell, and a ring of light drives back the swarm below. Not yet, Operator. My wall still stands.
The rift closes like an eye. Declined, with forty-one seconds left.
The hope drains out of Jaeha's face. Wait. Please wait.
He shouts a better offer. Fifty percent of every core! Two more rifts go grey.
Back in the room, Nib has gone stiff, ears flat. What is it, Seoa asks. What's that sound? He knows that bell.
One by one, the rifts go dark. Thirty-five seconds.
So he does what four years of contracts taught him: he scrolls down. Nobody ever reads the fine print.
The terms. The called hear his offer, and the heart under it. He can change it until the clock hits zero. If nobody accepts, the call is wasted, and Route Alignment drops back to zero.
His eyes widen. They hear the heart under it. And his heart wrote a job advert.
He remembers what Nib said. You were standing in front of someone.
Then the still water trembles, and something long and many-jointed rises beneath his feet. Twenty-eight seconds.
A black hand with too many joints clamps round his ankle, frost racing up his leg.
The window glitches red and blue. Warning: unregistered listener. Operator number one, status: hushed.
In the room, frost explodes across the floor from his foot.
Outside the window, Gomi arches her back and hisses at the glow.
The hand drags him to his knees. If it pulls him under, he doesn't think he comes back. Twenty seconds.
He tears the job advert out of his notebook.
And lets it sink.
He stops fighting, straightens up, and faces the dark rifts with nothing to read from. He can't pay what they're worth, or promise they'll win.
But he won't send them in alone. Whatever hits them, he'll carry half of it.
And everyone comes back. That's the only rule he has.
Back in the room, Nib's notched ear lifts, and the corner of his mouth almost smiles.
The last few lines to the rifts flicker brighter. Offer changed, with twelve seconds left.
Ten seconds. Jaeha closes his eyes.
Seven. The rifts stay dark, and the hand drags him to his waist.
In the room, Seoa holds his frost-white hand against her forehead.
Five. He's chest-deep, his breath fogging, still watching the rifts.
Four seconds of darkness.
Three. Then the mossy rift glows, and the long, flowered hill rises as if breathing. Something like a huge shoulder lifts.
And in the moss, two huge, slow amber eyes begin to open.
